worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{{x}^{n}}{{2}^{n/2}{n}^{4}}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{x}^{n+1}}{{2}^{(n+1)/2}(n+1)^{4}}\cdot \frac{{2}^{n/2}{n}^{4}}{{x}^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{x{n}^{4}}{{2}^{1/2}(n+1)^{4}}| \\  & =\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{2}}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{n}{n+1})}^{4} \\  & =\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for $|x|<\sqrt{2}.$ So, the radius of convergence is $\sqrt{2},$ and the series converges for any $x$ that lies in the open interval $(-\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2}).$

The ratio test gives no conclusion about the convergence of the series when $L=1.$ So, when $|x|=\sqrt{2},$ we do not know if the series converges. This means that the endpoints $x=-\sqrt{2}$ and $x=\sqrt{2}$ need to be investigated separately using another test for convergence.

- When $x=\sqrt{2}$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{2}^{n/2}{n}^{4}} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(\sqrt{2})^{n}}{{2}^{n/2}{n}^{4}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{2}^{n/2}}{{2}^{n/2}{n}^{4}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{n}^{4}}=1+\frac{1}{{2}^{4}}+\frac{1}{{3}^{4}}+\frac{1}{{4}^{4}}+⋯\,,\end{aligned}
$$

which is convergent by the $p$-series test.  So the endpoint $x=\sqrt{2}$ is included in our interval.

- When $x=-\sqrt{2}$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{2}^{n/2}{n}^{4}} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-\sqrt{2})^{n}}{{2}^{n/2}{n}^{4}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}{2}^{n/2}}{{2}^{n/2}{n}^{4}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{4}}=-1+\frac{1}{{2}^{4}}-\frac{1}{{3}^{4}}+\frac{1}{{4}^{4}}+⋯\,,\end{aligned}
$$

which is convergent by the alternating series test.  So the endpoint $x=-\sqrt{2}$ is included in our interval.

Therefore, the interval of convergence is $[-\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2}].$
